name: Victoria
tagline: Butchart Gardens, Mild Pacific Breezes, and Island Living North of the Border
description: Victoria sits at the southern tip of Vancouver Island, offering Canada's mildest climate, English-style gardens, and a relaxed island pace of life. With universal healthcare, a walkable inner harbor, thriving farm-to-table dining, and year-round outdoor recreation, Victoria delivers exceptional quality of life for retirees who want natural beauty without harsh winters. Housing is pricier than most Canadian cities but still well below Vancouver.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for Canadian citizens. Others: Super Visa (for parents/grandparents, up to 5 years) or Visitor Record extensions. No dedicated retirement visa — Canada lacks a retiree-specific immigration pathway.
quickFacts.safetyRating: Very Safe — consistently ranked among Canada's safest cities
quickFacts.nearestAirport: Victoria International Airport (YYJ) — 30 min from downtown
quickFacts.climate: Mild maritime Mediterranean with warm, dry summers and cool, rainy winters. Rarely drops below freezing. Canada's mildest city.

housing.description: Studio or older one-bedroom in Esquimalt or Saanich, off the tourist harbour

dining.description: Mostly home cooking with local farm produce; fish-and-chips and pub meals

healthcare.description: BC MSP covers essentials; basic dental-vision-prescription supplement

transportation.description: BC Transit monthly pass (C$85); Victoria is very bikeable

entertainment.description: Beacon Hill Park, free harbour strolls, shore whale-watching, library events

1M.lifestyle: A studio or older one-bedroom in Esquimalt or Saanich, off the tourist harbour but well-connected by bus and bike — Victoria's cycling infrastructure makes a car optional at this tier. Most meals are cooked at home with local farm produce, with fish-and-chips on the wharf or a casual pub meal as the treat. BC's MSP covers the essentials, leaving a basic dental-and-prescription supplement, and the mild coastal climate keeps heating costs down. Beacon Hill Park, free harbour strolls, and shore-based whale watching carry the leisure budget. Housing is the pressure point — Victoria's rents run close to Vancouver's — but the mild, nearly snow-free winters are a real reward.

housing.description: Proper one-bedroom in walkable James Bay or Fairfield

dining.description: Regular farm-to-table dining and weekend brunches in Oak Bay

healthcare.description: MSP plus private supplemental (dental, vision, massage)

transportation.description: A reliable car for island exploration plus BC Ferries trips

entertainment.description: Museum membership, kayaking the Gorge, whale-watching tours, live music

2M.lifestyle: A proper one-bedroom in walkable James Bay or Fairfield, within reach of the Inner Harbour, with regular farm-to-table dining, a car for island exploration and BC Ferries trips, and private supplemental cover. Year-round cycling and gardening, a strong craft-brewery-and-music scene, and a mild climate make for an easy, comfortable island routine.

housing.description: Nicer one-bedroom, character unit, or Inner-Harbour condo in Oak Bay

dining.description: Frequent fine dining at rooms like Brasserie L'École and Stage Wine Bar

healthcare.description: MSP plus comprehensive private cover with executive screening

transportation.description: A late-model car, ferries, and occasional floatplane to Vancouver

entertainment.description: Golf-club membership, sailing the Strait of Juan de Fuca, opera season tickets

3M.lifestyle: A nicer one-bedroom, character-home unit, or Inner-Harbour condo in Oak Bay or downtown, with fine dining at rooms like Brasserie L'École and Stage Wine Bar. A late-model car, regular BC Ferries or floatplane trips to Vancouver, and comprehensive private cover round out the essentials, while Cowichan Valley winery tours, sailing the Strait of Juan de Fuca, and golf are easy weekend activities. This is a comfortable, mild-climate island life with solid discretionary margin.

housing.description: Luxury one-bedroom or junior-two-bedroom waterfront unit

dining.description: Fine dining as routine plus a curated BC wine collection

healthcare.description: MSP plus executive-health, naturopathic, and premium private supplements

transportation.description: A luxury SUV plus Harbour Air floatplane commutes

entertainment.description: Yacht-club membership, private sailing, art collecting, symphony patronage

domesticHelp.description: Weekly housekeeping plus a gardener for the grounds

luxuryExtras.description: A Gulf Island cottage, quarterly international travel, boat moorage

5M.lifestyle: A luxury one-bedroom or junior-two-bedroom waterfront unit, frequent fine dining, a nice car, floatplane commutes, and a weekly housekeeper. Yacht-club membership, a Gulf Island cottage, boat moorage, and premium private cover put this firmly into upscale coastal island living.

housing.description: Prime waterfront luxury apartment in the Uplands / Cordova Bay tier

dining.description: Near-daily fine dining and private supper-club and winery events

healthcare.description: MSP plus concierge medicine and international medical cover

transportation.description: Multiple luxury vehicles and a private floatplane charter

entertainment.description: Major arts philanthropy, private regattas, exclusive golf-and-yacht memberships

domesticHelp.description: Full domestic help — housekeeper, gardener, property manager

luxuryExtras.description: Multiple Gulf Island properties, a private boat, a charitable foundation, bespoke travel

10M.lifestyle: A prime waterfront luxury apartment in the Uplands or Cordova Bay tier, near-daily fine dining, a luxury vehicle, and a private floatplane charter or boat for Gulf Island days. Full domestic help, concierge and international-grade private cover, and yacht-and-golf-club access define the ceiling. Victoria is a small city with limited luxury infrastructure, so much of this tier funds travel, boating, and the quiet prestige of a mild-climate waterfront address rather than big-city extravagance.
